::: {.route-question}
Question for today: CellCo's cathode coating varies from coupon to coupon. Which variation should an operator react to, and can the gauge be trusted to tell?
:::

## The coating line {#coating}

::: {.two}
::: {}
A slot die spreads cathode slurry on aluminum foil, which then dries in a long oven. The **mass loading** decides how much energy each cell stores.

**Target:** 20.0 mg/cm². **Specification:** 19.4 to 20.6 mg/cm².

Every hour, five coupons are punched across the web and weighed.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
In Block 1, 93.3% of the cells that entered formation ended good. Today we look further upstream, at the coating line, where many defects start.
:::
:::
:::

## Common and special causes {#causes}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Common-cause variation** comes from many small sources always present: slurry viscosity, foil thickness, oven airflow. It is the process's own noise. Reducing it needs a change to the system.

**Special-cause variation** comes from an identifiable event: a clogged die lip, a new slurry batch, a tension fault. It should be found and removed.
:::
::: {}
**Two mistakes**

Reacting to common-cause variation as if it were special (tampering) adds variation.

Ignoring a special cause lets a fault run.

A control chart separates the two, with limits set by the process's own common-cause variation, not by the specification.
:::
:::

## Tampering adds variation {#tampering data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="tpx">
  <div class="w-controls"><span class="w-toggle" role="group" aria-label="Operator rule">
    <button type="button" data-m="0" aria-pressed="true">Leave the die alone</button><button type="button" data-m="1" aria-pressed="false">Adjust after every coupon</button></span></div>
  <svg id="tpx-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 270" role="img" aria-label="Fifty coupon mass loadings under the chosen operator rule"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="tpx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('tpx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const e = [0.351,-0.440,0.072,-0.098,-0.078,-0.037,-0.347,-0.040,-0.149,0.572,0.039,-0.061,-0.048,-0.115,-0.181,-0.067,0.083,-0.041,0.165,-0.034,0.004,0.266,0.094,-0.087,-0.031,0.093,0.333,-0.046,-0.042,0.172,-0.152,-0.050,0.152,0.100,0.016,0.115,-0.486,0.176,-0.165,-0.287,0.048,0.120,-0.077,-0.185,0.004,-0.009,0.242,0.129,0.033,0.191];
  function series(m) { let adj = 0; return e.map((v) => { const x = 20 + adj + v; if (m) adj -= x - 20; return x; }); }
  const sd = (a) => { const mu = a.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / a.length; return Math.sqrt(a.reduce((s, v) => s + (v - mu) ** 2, 0) / (a.length - 1)); };
  function draw(m) {
    const xs = series(m), W = 1160, H = 270, L = 70, R = 20, T = 10, B = 34, X = (i) => L + i / 49 * (W - L - R), Y = (v) => T + (1 - (v - 19.0) / 2.0) * (H - T - B);
    let g = '';
    for (const v of [19.0, 19.4, 20.0, 20.6, 21.0]) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${Y(v)}" y2="${Y(v)}" stroke="${v === 19.4 || v === 20.6 ? '#BE654C' : '#B9C1C6'}" ${v === 19.4 || v === 20.6 ? 'stroke-dasharray="7 5" stroke-width="2"' : ''}/><text x="${L - 8}" y="${Y(v) + 5}" text-anchor="end" font-size="15" fill="#333F4A">${v.toFixed(1)}</text>`;
    let p = ''; xs.forEach((v, i) => { p += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(i).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(v).toFixed(1); });
    g += `<path d="${p}" fill="none" stroke="${m ? '#E29A2D' : '#0F6E6B'}" stroke-width="2"/>` + xs.map((v, i) => `<circle cx="${X(i)}" cy="${Y(v)}" r="4" fill="${m ? '#E29A2D' : '#0F6E6B'}"/>`).join('');
    g += `<text x="${W - R}" y="${Y(20.6) - 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="15" fill="#BE654C">Specification limits</text><text x="${L + 6}" y="${H - 8}" font-size="15" fill="#333F4A">Coupon 1 to 50</text>`;
    const out = xs.filter((v) => v < 19.4 || v > 20.6).length;
    document.getElementById('tpx-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('tpx-out').innerHTML = `Standard deviation: <span class="best">${sd(xs).toFixed(3)} mg/cm²</span>. Coupons outside specification: ${out} of 50.` + (m ? ' The operator moves the die by the last error each time, so each correction carries the last coupon\'s noise into the next.' : '');
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-m]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => { root.querySelectorAll('[data-m]').forEach((q) => q.setAttribute('aria-pressed', q === b)); draw(+b.dataset.m); }));
  draw(0);
})();
</script>
```

[Same noise in both runs. Adjusting after every coupon raises the standard deviation from 0.19 to 0.29 mg/cm²; in theory by a factor of √2.]{.hint}

:::
::: {}
Coating defects (loading, streaks, pinholes, edges) are **36%** of all defects; with slitting burrs, **60%**.

A Pareto chart ranks problems so that effort goes to the few that matter. It counts defects, not their cost: if a weld defect costs ten times a burr, rank by cost as well.

[Mass loading, the key coating variable, is today's case. Before charting it, we must check the gauge.]{.hint}
:::
:::

## Measurement system analysis {#gage}

::: {.two}
::: {}
Observed variation = part-to-part variation + measurement variation.

σ²~total~ = σ²~part~ + σ²~GRR~, with σ²~GRR~ = σ²~repeatability~ + σ²~reproducibility~

**Repeatability:** one operator, same part, same gauge, repeated readings.

**Reproducibility:** different operators measuring the same parts.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>%GRR</th><th>Verdict</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Below 10%</td><td>Acceptable</td></tr>
    <tr><td>10% to 30%</td><td>Marginal: depends on use and cost</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Above 30%</td><td>Unacceptable: fix the gauge first</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
%GRR = σ~GRR~ / σ~total~. Number of distinct categories, ndc = 1.41 σ~part~ / σ~GRR~, should be at least 5.
:::
:::

## Explore a gauge study {#gage-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="grx">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">Repeatability σ <strong id="grx-ev">0.012</strong><input type="range" id="grx-e" min="0.002" max="0.08" step="0.002" value="0.012"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">Reproducibility σ <strong id="grx-ov">0.008</strong><input type="range" id="grx-o" min="0" max="0.08" step="0.002" value="0.008"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">Part-to-part σ <strong id="grx-pv">0.170</strong><input type="range" id="grx-p" min="0.02" max="0.3" step="0.005" value="0.17"></label>
  </div>
  <svg id="grx-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 150" role="img" aria-label="Share of total variation from the gauge and from the parts"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="grx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('grx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  function draw() {
    const e = +document.getElementById('grx-e').value, o = +document.getElementById('grx-o').value, p = +document.getElementById('grx-p').value;
    document.getElementById('grx-ev').textContent = e.toFixed(3); document.getElementById('grx-ov').textContent = o.toFixed(3); document.getElementById('grx-pv').textContent = p.toFixed(3);
    const grr = Math.hypot(e, o), tot = Math.hypot(grr, p), pct = 100 * grr / tot, ndc = Math.floor(1.41 * p / grr);
    const verdict = pct < 10 ? 'acceptable' : pct <= 30 ? 'marginal' : 'unacceptable', col = pct < 10 ? '#0F6E6B' : pct <= 30 ? '#E29A2D' : '#BE654C';
    const W = 1100, L = 30, X = (v) => L + v / 100 * W;
    let g = `<rect x="${L}" y="30" width="${W}" height="40" fill="#B9C1C6" opacity="0.5"/><rect x="${L}" y="30" width="${X(pct) - L}" height="40" fill="${col}"/>`;
    for (const v of [10, 30]) g += `<line x1="${X(v)}" x2="${X(v)}" y1="22" y2="78" stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><text x="${X(v)}" y="16" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" fill="#333F4A">${v}%</text>`;
    g += `<text x="${L}" y="104" font-size="16" fill="#1C242B">%GRR (share of total standard deviation due to the gauge)</text>`;
    document.getElementById('grx-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('grx-out').innerHTML = `σ<sub>GRR</sub> = ${grr.toFixed(4)}, %GRR = <span class="best">${pct.toFixed(1)}%</span>, ${verdict}; ndc = ${ndc}${ndc < 5 ? ' (too few to separate parts)' : ''}.`;
  }
  root.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[CellCo's coating gauge: repeatability 0.012, reproducibility 0.008, parts 0.170 mg/cm². %GRR 8.5%, ndc 16: fit for charting. Now shrink the part-to-part spread: the same gauge becomes useless.]{.hint}

## Activity · Classroom Gage R&R {#act1 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Individual, then whole class · 30 minutes · measurements and the measurement share]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Measure the 10 printed line segments twice with your ruler, in millimeters to one decimal. Cover your first readings before the second round.
:::

1. **Repeatability:** for each segment, take the difference between your two readings. Average the 10 differences, then divide by 1.128.
2. **Reproducibility:** enter your mean of all 20 readings in the class sheet. The standard deviation of the class means estimates it.
3. **Parts:** the standard deviation of the 10 segment means over the whole class.
4. Compute %GRR and ndc. Is a ruler fit to tell these segments apart?

## Activity · What to look for {#act1-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Resolution.** A ruler reads to 0.5 or 1 mm. If the segments differ by only 1 to 2 mm, the ruler's resolution alone pushes %GRR toward the marginal range. Rule of ten: resolution at most one tenth of the spread you need to see.

**Reproducibility.** Different starting points (zero mark or ruler edge) and viewing angles show up as differences between students' means.
:::
::: {}
**What it means for CellCo.** A coating chart built on a poor gauge shows gauge noise as process variation: limits too wide, real shifts hidden.

**Order of work.** Check the gauge, then chart the process, then compute capability. Session 16 charts the coating data; Session 17 computes capability.
:::
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
Common-cause variation is the system's noise; special causes are events to find. Tampering with a stable process adds variation.
:::
::: {.tk}
Pareto charts aim effort: two defect types make 60% of CellCo's defects, led by coating.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
Check the gauge before charting. CellCo's coating gauge has %GRR 8.5% and ndc 16: fit for use.
:::
:::

[Session 16: control charts for the coating line, including charts for small drifts.]{.note-line}

| English | 中文 | English | 中文 |

| Special-cause variation | 特殊原因变异 | Cause-and-effect diagram | 因果图（鱼骨图） |
| Measurement system analysis | 测量系统分析 | Repeatability, reproducibility | 重复性、再现性 |
